newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat shrugs off export woes, surges late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat shrugs off export woes, surges late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures shrugged off their earlier export-induced funk and closed mostly higher in a late rally, traders said.
"The market was poised to make a bit of a bounce and it got real carried away. We saw the tip of some domestic (mill-related) buying late and then we triggered some buy stops," a trader said.

Some traders said the late buying in KCBT wheat was linked to the sudden jump in basis levels at Cargill's flour mill locations in eastern Kansas. Overall, Cargill bought one million KCBT Dec bushels during Thursday's session.

But other traders said the rally was done more on fund-related buying than anything else. They cited Refco's purchase of two million March bushels -- most of it coming in last 20 minutes of the session.
KCBT wheat closed two cents lower to seven cents higher, with Dec up seven cents at $4.43 a bushel. March gained seven cents to close at $3.96.
KCBT July wheat set a new contract low at $3.35 before being swept higher by the late rally.
Traders said wheat values had fallen to their intraday lows at the midsession amid concern that U.S. wheat was priced too high for global export business.
Apart from the late buying by Cargill and Refco, volumes were mostly lackluster throughout the session. Term Commodities bought one million July bushels, traders said.
